# Package API, Declarations, and Migration Ledger

This page is generated from all 34 public manifests, package documentation, and
`governance/package-release-notes.json`. It records source candidates without
publishing them. CI rejects a version change unless its release classification,
summary, and migration guidance are updated at the same time.

The declaration targets below describe the packed manifest contract. The
package pages remain the human API and usage authority; generated declarations
and clean-consumer tests remain the executable type authority.

| `@bsv/402-pay`                    | `0.3.2`      | `0.3.3`  | patch     | [API and usage](../packages/middleware/402-pay.md)                    | Custom clients must send a strictly framed BRC-95 Atomic BEEF envelope whose subject is the payment transaction; plain BEEF is no longer accepted. Legacy Atomic BEEF containing unrelated branches remains compatible because the server reduces it to the declared subject and dependency closure. The default replay store is bounded and process-local; production services with more than one serving process or node must inject the same durable atomic PaymentReplayStore everywhere. Low-level validators should retain one wallet object or pass an explicit store. Applications that relied on implicit console diagnostics must supply the optional structured logger. Treat an unchallenged 503 after payment submission as ambiguous and reconcile the transaction before requesting another payment. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. | `@bsv/auth`                       | `0.1.5`      | `0.1.6`  | patch     | [API and usage](../packages/middleware/auth.md)                       | No valid proof bytes or public API shape changes. Client and server must use the same protocol tuple; security levels 0, 1, and 2 remain supported and select wallet consent policy while the explicit counterparty scopes derivation at every level. Proof and wallet adapters must supply plain own data fields and dense byte arrays; inherited, accessor-backed, sparse, or malformed runtime shapes fail closed. Structured bodies containing non-finite numbers or negative zero must be normalized to an unambiguous wire representation before signing. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. | `@bsv/auth-express-middleware`    | `2.2.8`      | `2.3.0`  | minor     | [API and usage](../packages/middleware/auth-express-middleware.md)    | No change for ordinary routes. Guarded routes explicitly call guardAuthenticatedResponse after authentication and before sending; acquire the application durable fence, recheck current authorization and targets, and synchronously enqueue under it. Persist the returned plan and every partial settlement proof, retry with the same funded transaction, and configure a profile-aware agreementEvaluator before completion or recovery. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with the package; published BRC-170 remains authoritative if the implementation and standard differ. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. The optional overlay-acquisition entry requires the coordinated SDK3 output and revenue-listing companions. Ordinary BRC-170 imports and SDK2 consumers remain unchanged. Decoded acquisition context and entitlement fingerprints remain explicitly unverified. Opt-in callers must install local proof sources and protected immutable-object custody before funding. LCHOverlayPaidDomain performs the concrete fixed-render/direct-collector checks; unsupported policy terms and profiles fail before funding. Ordinary BRC-170 imports, CORE_CAPABILITIES and SDK2 peers stay unchanged. The minor candidate adds APIs and a locally qualified authenticated native paid-lookup recovery flow. The operator workbench and covenant acquisition demonstrations remain checkpoint-two work. Install LCHOverlayPaidSeller only with the protected coordinator, actual read-only native credit reconciliation and complete original CEKs; financial effects remain owned by the coordinator and native adapters. Opt-in covenant callers must compose the terms adapter with actual complete genesis/Script/purchase, role and release verification; terms validation alone cannot issue a License or authorize decryption. Preserve the buyer-free standing Offer and exact original signed Request on every retry. Import LCHOverlayCovenantDomain through @bsv/lch/overlay-covenant, reserve original and positive-verification custody before financial work, and install actual full lineage/purchase/release proof ports. A decoded portable package, signed settlement or entitlement fingerprint alone cannot authorize playback. Public disclosed native buyer fixtures execute the real covenant and encrypted custody; the combined native wallet/seller/admission workbench remains an open checkpoint requirement. Install LCHOverlayCovenantSeller with actual full verifiers and the protected purchase coordinator; the advertised finite request/response limits must reserve the complete future C context before preparation. Issuance requires the complete retained candidate passed by the current coordinator, independently assessed release and original private material. Catalogue withdrawal does not replace that obligation. Combined wallet-backed topical-admission and operator demonstrations remain in progress. The opt-in covenant domain accepts complete plain BEEF selected by the original explicit wallet txid, independent of proof-record order; present Atomic BEEF markers must match. All original independent material, Script, lineage and licence checks remain. Ordinary BRC-170 behavior and persisted formats are unchanged. Existing BRC170 and paid-lookup behavior is unchanged. The approved pre-adoption C profile replacement requires purchaseCommitment in its signed settlement and in installed purchase verifier results; return the full authenticated input-zero SHA256d digest with an owned synchronous checkCurrent guard. Never infer it from equal outputs or transport claims. Preserve original signed release, License, settlement and protected obligations; currentAlias is separate unverified transport evidence. Qualify the replacement family, immutable collector terms, protected child wallet and native alias custody before advertising C. No existing ordinary content or paid-lookup stored format is reinterpreted. For current C representation, select decodeLCHCollectorRevenueProfile/bindLCHCollectorRevenueProfile and supply the exact immutable schedule and expiryHeight. New preparations require independently verified active stage and installed current height below expiry; retained obligations do not repeat that new-work predicate. These helpers do not authenticate Offers, verify ancestry/currentness or migrate the historical buyer/seller/native alias owners; full integration remains checkpoint work. Authenticate current C with validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfileTerms and retain its original consent; validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfilePromise validates a frozen obligation, while validateLCHOverlayCovenantProfileWindow is for new work. Independently verify authorized current-family lineage, roles, active stage and installed chain height before financial work. These terms interfaces perform no wallet action and do not migrate the historical buyer/seller/native alias owners. Select decodeLCHOverlayCovenantProfilePurchaseEvidence and bindLCHOverlayCovenantProfileSettlement for the current immutable descriptor. Representation and signed commitment binding do not establish actual Bitcoin history, Script execution, roles, release satisfaction, License validity or native alias ownership; retain independent full verification and historical entitlement checks. Select LCHOverlayCovenantProfileDomain for the current immutable collector. Initialize protected custody and retain/recheck fundingPreflight immediately before financial effects. Install actual complete current lineage, original funded and released transaction proof, and release-policy ports. Existing historical domain IDs/formats/defaults remain unchanged; retained delivery and offline playback never repeat a new-funding expiry predicate. Native alias/action custody and current seller integration remain separate required work. Select LCHOverlayCovenantProfileSeller for current immutable seller material. Its distinct installation identity does not reinterpret historical custody. Supply complete actual reserve/activation/purchase/release verifiers; retain and recheck the preparation guard before promising material. Original historical seller interfaces/IDs/formats/defaults remain. Current coordinator commitment packets and native alias/action/admission/HTTP composition remain separate integration requirements. Use configurePrivatePurchase or the private-purchase router before body parsers, and supply a durable coordinator/disclosure owner. The application drains its outstanding work before closing protected custody. Basic transport refusal precedes authentication and private work. Use allowPayments: false for unpaid authenticated requests. Use HTTPS for confidentiality. Omitted controls preserve existing behavior. OutputLookupTransport is opt-in: persist the original opening before dispatch, and atomically commit each batch with its cursor before reading further. Full durable service/runtime integration is separate; no default legacy behavior changes. They do not implement protected storage, wallet internalizeOnce, transaction/release eligibility or secret usability; legacy BRC-105 and lookup context are unchanged. Payment funding inspection requires an independently derived seller payment key, selected chain and retained quote; it does not establish Bitcoin acceptance, reserve an acquisition or internalize wallet value. Enforce total HTTP header limits and use a separate durable idempotent wallet adapter before acknowledging credit. Root-eviction helpers are opt-in and require independently authenticated context, the original signed request and retained evaluation policy. Check clocks only when accepting new requests; retained outcomes remain recoverable under current access policy. Evidence verification, local authority, durable tombstones and every serving/replay guard remain service obligations. Existing SHIP/SLAP, lookup and GASP behavior is unchanged. No migration for existing lookup consumers. Persist original root operation/selection/policy together before constructing OutputRootEvictionTransport; supply trusted root/base/chain/rules and a wallet. The client retries that operation or reads its original status without discovery, persistence, automatic polling or payment. Current access and all serving/evidence decisions remain separate server obligations. Persist the exact proposal request and fresh selected contract before constructing OutputProposalTransport. Each send retries only that saved request. Finalize returns response plus matchesRequest: a different existing reservation is not fulfillment of the requested transaction. Local transport errors remain distinct from authenticated OutputProposalServiceError; domain/evidence verification, current authority, persistence and new-operation freshness remain explicit caller and provider obligations. Existing AuthFetch defaults stay unchanged. Select the new transport explicitly and retain original contracts and payment bytes in a durable owner; see the paid lookup client guide. Existing verification and freshness/authority APIs are unchanged; callers still perform every role, expiry, policy and current-context check. The bounded caches have no persistent data or migration. OutputPurchaseTransport is explicitly selected and requires retained original capability/request/terms and a recipient authentication wallet. Compose durable custody and explicit new-work authorization separately; finite transport never constructs, pays, signs, broadcasts or validates Script/usable private material. The additive ownOutputJSON utility accepts JavaScript values, including strings as values; use parseOutputJSON for incoming JSON text or UTF-8 bytes. Schema, current authorization, wire and storage contracts remain unchanged. The response-waiter lifecycle correction changes no wire format, public API, deadline, automatic payment or session-recovery defaults. Updated opt-in BRC-197 purchases require purchaseCommitment in every reserved result and POTATOES. Pass the independently verified full preimage digest to verifyOutputPurchaseEnvelope as its optional fourth argument; this never relaxes historical txid checks. The additive authorization callback requires independently verified local policy; wallet-returned labels or fields are not authority. Web request decoding rejects duplicate members and invalid UTF8, and custom parsed-body adapters must establish equivalent strict decoding. Preserve received text and inspect verification.verified, not HTTP success. Local revocation record status is retained/unknown, not inferred chain revocation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. Replace createServerWalletHandler() deployments with createServerWalletHandler({ authorize: async ({ action, headers }) => authenticatedSessionCanUseAction(headers, action) }). The callback must return literal true for each status, create, request, receive, balance, outputs, or reset action; omission now returns HTTP 403 for every action. Roll out the authentication layer and callback with the package, update anonymous probes or automation, and apply the same policy to every replica. Do not emulate the old public behavior with an unconditional authorize: () => true callback. Valid recipient derivations and authenticated Message Box peers remain supported; malformed, wrong-owner, or transaction-mutated flows now fail closed. New CredentialSchema and Certifier records use canonical 32-byte types. Current SDK wallet methods reject historical short types, so do not put migration aliases in wallet list, acquire, prove, or relinquish calls. Export affected records through the storage version that created them, authenticate them offline against the exact locally configured identifier, and reissue/import canonical replacements; no legacy certificate is rewritten automatically. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/. Persisted local field ordering requires no migration; transport adapters preserve original certificate signing bytes. Removed exports: MandalaToken, MandalaTokenDecoded, MandalaAdmin, ADMIN_PROTOCOL, MandalaAdminDecoded, MandalaActionDetails, MandalaActionKind, MandalaAdminLockParams, MandalaAdminUnlockParams and AssetMetadata. Removed subpath @bsv/templates/mandala-signing.ts. The @bsv/templates/mandala-encoding.ts subpath keeps only createMinimallyEncodedScriptChunk, decodeScriptNum and decodeScriptNumChunk; encodeScriptNum, encodeAssetId and decodeAssetId are removed. Replace MandalaToken/MandalaAdmin with Bsv21Binary: deploy, authority and value outputs are lock(tokenId \| null, amount, pubKeyHash, payload?) with bigint amounts and <txid>_0 token ids (tokenIdFromString/tokenIdToString), decoded with Bsv21Binary.decode. Mandala admin actions are committed by sha256 of strict-CBOR details in the authority output payload, not by a commitment-derived key. This is a clean break with no data migration: tokens and admin chains in the old format are not readable by 2.0.0. @bsv/overlay-topics 2.0.0 consumes this format; the infra/overlay-server wiring follows after publication. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the SDK3 candidate; SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API (see docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md). Pending no-send actions and retryable failures retain the same originator-bound abort behavior; positively queued or broadcast actions no longer retain session ownership records. Upgrade the SDK to a release exposing completeBoundAction.outputAuthorizationVersion=1 alongside wallet-toolbox 2.14.6. SDK2 peers keep their existing strict behavior; they do not obtain this fee-bearing faucet fix. The main SDK3.1 candidate retains the separate SDK3 retirement migration; SDK2 hosts require a coordinated additive backport or that migration. Serialized or cross-package-instance result adapters discard local authority and fail closed. Signup interruption/retry persistence is unchanged; reconcile any previous faucet transaction before repeating a failed signup. No API or schema migration is required for pin continuity. Retire a support pin only after unpinned lookup independently returns the verified current token. Deploy overlay 2.6.4 plus overlay-topics 2.0.1 or an equivalent history decider for confirmed ancestry. Stored WAB pins remain lineage anchors; the client follows verified descendants without needing an administrative pin rewrite. For ordinary callers, no public API, wire, database, or consumer migration is required. Recovery adoption requires SDK 3.0.0, explicit auxiliary schema installation in the active local SQLite wallet, stable operation IDs and a committed workspace. Reopen retained state after restart; never silently reinstall a missing journal. These journals are outside legacy entity snapshots, BRC-38/39 export, ordinary sync, IndexedDB and remote providers. Back up the whole consistent wallet database plus keys and test restoration. For rollback, stop new adoption and reconcile outstanding operations with the original controller before removing it; preserve journals and keys. Local receipts do not establish quote-time capacity, settlement, domain authority or protected delivery. The private encoder extraction requires no caller or stored-format migration; complete canonical mutation qualification covers every helper. Existing callers can omit checkNewSigning. The optional callback returns void synchronously or throws, and cannot undo or timestamp already-started storage effects; reconcile the original operation after uncertainty. This internal ownership refactor changes no accepted bytes, public action API, stored schema, errors or caller defaults; no additional migration is required and context is never retained between calls. BRC-197 integrations must explicitly select getBrc197InternalizationCapabilities and internalizeBrc197Action with the literal fixed remittance fields; do not Base64-encode them or route them through ordinary internalizeAction. Validate every recipient and the complete protected activation/signing, lineage, chain, fee and resource prerequisites before funding a listing. See docs/guides/brc197-fixed-child-wallet.md for the local-only boundary and outstanding qualification gates. `none` means the source manifest matches the recorded npm baseline. Any other
value is an unpublished candidate. `initial` with a null published baseline
identifies a new package with no recorded published baseline; it does not invent an npm
version or waive publication checks. Publication, tags, releases, registry
reconciliation, and infrastructure dependency synchronization remain separate,
explicitly authorized operations.

## Package entry points

## @bsv/402-pay

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/middleware/402-pay.md](../packages/middleware/402-pay.md)
- Source: [packages/middleware/402-pay](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/middleware/402-pay)
- Release note: Adds an exact-tarball Vite and esbuild contract for the browser-safe client entry point, including a bundle-size ratchet and an assertion that server exports never leak into browser consumers. Retains the hash-pinned pre-uniformization Open BSV License version 4 grant as a scoped continuity notice. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Binds BRC-121 pricing and internalization to the transaction declared by the BRC-95 Atomic BEEF subject, removes unrelated included branches, rejects trailing bytes and non-atomic envelopes, and requires affirmative wallet acceptance before serving paid content. Adds independent bounded atomic transaction replay claims so conforming BRC-100 wallets that omit the non-public isMerge detail cannot authorize duplicate access, preserves actual overpayments in middleware receipts, uses fixed bounded wallet descriptions, makes diagnostics opt-in, and returns an unchallenged 503 after ambiguous wallet or replay-store failures to avoid inducing a second spend. Aligns the development-only Vitest runner and V8 coverage provider at 4.1.11. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: Custom clients must send a strictly framed BRC-95 Atomic BEEF envelope whose subject is the payment transaction; plain BEEF is no longer accepted. Legacy Atomic BEEF containing unrelated branches remains compatible because the server reduces it to the declared subject and dependency closure. The default replay store is bounded and process-local; production services with more than one serving process or node must inject the same durable atomic PaymentReplayStore everywhere. Low-level validators should retain one wallet object or pass an explicit store. Applications that relied on implicit console diagnostics must supply the optional structured logger. Treat an unchallenged 503 after payment submission as ambiguous and reconcile the transaction before requesting another payment. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

| Public subpath | Runtime target(s)                          | Declaration target(s)                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `.`            | `./dist/index.mjs`<br>`./dist/index.cjs`   | `./dist/index.d.mts`<br>`./dist/index.d.cts`   |
| `./server`     | `./dist/server.mjs`<br>`./dist/server.cjs` | `./dist/server.d.mts`<br>`./dist/server.d.cts` |
| `./client`     | `./dist/client.mjs`<br>`./dist/client.cjs` | `./dist/client.d.mts`<br>`./dist/client.d.cts` |

## @bsv/air-gap

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/helpers/air-gap.md](../packages/helpers/air-gap.md)
- Source: [packages/helpers/air-gap](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/helpers/air-gap)
- Release note: Bounds BRC-141 decoder state, scanned strings, duplicate tracking, pending mixes, fountain indices, and high-degree work while replacing sparse O(K) index materialization with bounded mapping. Systematic and degree-one frames remain available under pressure and valid wire-v1 payloads retain their bytes.
- Migration: No migration is required for valid BRC-141 v1 senders or decoders. Malformed, oversized, duplicate-heavy, or adversarial high-degree sessions now fail closed or are evicted within the documented limits instead of consuming unbounded resources.

| Public subpath | Runtime target(s)                        | Declaration target(s)                        |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `.`            | `./dist/index.mjs`<br>`./dist/index.cjs` | `./dist/index.d.mts`<br>`./dist/index.d.cts` |

## @bsv/amountinator

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/helpers/amountinator.md](../packages/helpers/amountinator.md)
- Source: [packages/helpers/amountinator](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/helpers/amountinator)
- Release note: Validates finite monetary values, normalized nonempty currency codes, integer decimal precision, grouping flags, converter rates, and conversion results, and formats negative sub-unit amounts from their absolute magnitude without losing the sign. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: Valid finite inputs retain the public API. Currency identifiers are trimmed and normalized to uppercase; callers that passed non-finite values, empty currencies, coercive options, invalid decimal precision, or non-finite converter results must normalize or reject them before calling because those values now fail closed. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

| Public subpath | Runtime target(s)                        | Declaration target(s)                        |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `.`            | `./dist/index.mjs`<br>`./dist/index.cjs` | `./dist/index.d.mts`<br>`./dist/index.d.cts` |

## @bsv/auth

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/middleware/auth.md](../packages/middleware/auth.md)
- Source: [packages/middleware/auth](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/middleware/auth)
- Release note: Adopts the governed strict TypeScript profile and repository-wide zero-warning lint and formatting contract. Snapshots canonical own-data proof fields, dense signature bytes, bodies, protocols, wallet identities, and exact wallet verdicts before asynchronous work; rejects accessor/inherited authority and ambiguous JSON numbers; and retains exact nonce-consumption replay claims. ## @bsv/message-box-client

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/messaging/message-box-client.md](../packages/messaging/message-box-client.md)
- Source: [packages/messaging/message-box-client](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/messaging/message-box-client)
- Release note: listMessages() and listMessagesLite() report paymentOutcome ('internalized', 'failed', 'skipped' or 'no-wallet-outputs') on each message that carried a payment, and keep that payment on the returned message unless the wallet accepted it (issue #503). Previously the payment envelope was always removed and a failed internalization was only logged, so acknowledging a listed message could delete the only copy of a payment. Both PeerMessage fields are optional and absent on messages without a payment. This release also carries the @bsv/sdk peer-floor raise from ^2.8.0 to ^2.8.6: SDK 2.8.0 through 2.8.5 derive the recipient key in Brc29RemittanceModule.acceptSettlement without forSelf, so PeerPayClient.acceptPayment() and rejectPayment() fail with brc29.internalize_failed for every valid incoming payment, and SDK 2.8.6 fixes acceptance. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: No migration required for the new fields: the PeerMessage paymentOutcome and retained payment are optional, and messages without a payment are unchanged. To avoid losing payments, store any returned payment (validate it first; it is the raw envelope value) before acknowledging its message. Install @bsv/sdk 2.8.6 or later alongside this package; payments refused on earlier SDKs remain pending in the message box and can be accepted after upgrading. No BRC100 wire or wallet-data change. SDK consumers may retain ^2.8.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

| `./package.json` | `./package.json`                    | —                                       |

Signed alias representation remains received until independent released-subject and usable-rights verification; historical recovery retains the first protected identity and never allocates a replacement wallet action. Select WalletToolboxProfilePurchasePayment explicitly with the current RevenueListingProfile and original recoverable action owner. Preserve its separately bound format-two plans and both program hashes; never reinterpret historical format-one custody or create another financial intent after a missing reply. Current native listing funding, fixed-child remittance, alias reconciliation and full HTTP integration remain separate requirements. Select RevenueListingProfileAuthority from the optional revenue-listing entry for the current family. Supply an independently chosen identity, explicit originator and synchronous current authorization fence; await actual child signing preflight before genesis funding. Independently approve the complete funded plan, lineage and roles. The adapter creates no funds or transaction and cannot undo an already produced wallet signature. Historical authority APIs, defaults, wire formats and custody remain unchanged; native all-route and combined release qualification remain checkpoint work. Internal alias companions introduce no public entry or stored-format migration. Historical exact-txid owners remain unchanged; source review and mutation registration do not qualify complete alias delivery.

## @bsv/overlay

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/overlays/overlay.md](../packages/overlays/overlay.md)
- Source: [packages/overlays/overlay](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/overlays/overlay)
- Release note: Maps SQL NULL output block heights to absent confirmation metadata without inventing a height or changing stored state. Strict engine height validation remains unchanged. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Explicit lookup history retains selected confirmed predecessors instead of truncating them at a Merkle proof; unrequested history and ordinary proof serialization are unchanged. Adds an optional retained-admission history contract and explicit Mongo retention. New opt-in commits preserve bounded immutable identity alongside the existing public receipt; trusted history reads bind applied topic, policy, context and operation after restart without asserting current unspentness or visibility. Legacy submission, receipt bytes and database validators remain unchanged. Adds the optional proposal-admission entry: an Engine bridge that recovers original retained topic receipts, isolates selected-topic disclosure, bounds physical concurrency and preflights complete result capacity before ordinary submission. Adds the optional private-publication-admission entry, using existing off-chain values and original retained public admission with explicit history-reuse policy, current installed-context guards, finite request/result/concurrency bounds and selected-output membership. Proposal and private adapters share the same original-assessment validator. Trusted opt-in retained admission history now supplies its original atomic server acceptance time, separately from unchanged ordinary receipt bytes; a timed selected-topic companion requires that provenance instead of substituting recovery time. Adds an optional selected-host OverlayPurchaseAdmission bridge restoring the original authenticated selection and original retained topic receipt/time after lost or duplicate submit replies. No private material enters ordinary Engine submission or GASP. Adds explicit bounded public BEEF ancestry retention for new atomic admissions, preserving raw ancestors below a current leaf proof. Adds separate node/topic-scoped historical output reads and opt-in pinned GASP history hydration; ordinary payload/read/serialization defaults stay unchanged.
- Migration: No wire, API, or database migration. Deploy the reviewed patch through the protected release workflow; retain existing validation and configured resource bounds. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. For UMP lineage, deploy this engine patch together with overlay-topics 2.0.1 or an equivalent custom UMP history decider. Existing selector decisions and resource bounds remain unchanged. None for existing consumers. To retain provenance for new commits, explicitly construct MongoOverlayStorage or MongoAdmissionStorage with retainAdmissionHistory: true. Existing receipts are not rewritten or retroactively certified; history remains unresolved when binding material is absent. Readers must authorize and project private multi-topic results. Disable the option to return to legacy writes; saved metadata remains compatible with legacy receipt readers. No database schema migration or deployment is performed. The new proposal-admission entry requires SDK 3.0 or newer, explicit retained-history storage and an installed immutable service/topic/rules binding. Existing root exports and SDK peer floors remain unchanged. Use it only behind ProposalService durable reservation, exact policy/transaction verification and authenticated access; missing history stays unresolved, and old receipts are not synthesized. Drain recovery calls before replacing Engine/storage/topic configuration. The new private-publication-admission entry requires SDK3, retained-history storage, an explicit public-history reuse policy and independent publisher/schema/Bitcoin validation plus durable reservation. It does not enable private HTTP, lookup readiness or paid delivery. Existing public submission and proposal behavior remain unchanged; no stored receipt is rewritten. Ordinary receipt and storage formats remain unchanged. Retained Mongo history reads the immutable committed operation timestamp. Legacy history providers may omit it; profiles requiring original time remain unavailable until that provenance exists, with no automatic reconstruction. Install the purchase-admission entry explicitly with topic rules, domain profile and admitted successor index. It requires independent domain validation and a reserved private intent; legacy receipt histories without original commit time cannot establish this stronger premise. Opt into retainedBEEF with a complete positive byte budget at most4MiB when original public ancestry is required. Older records without manifests preserve older reads; missing or damaged promised manifests fail closed. GASP historicalOutputs requires an explicit installed history port and supplies no current-membership or unspentness claim. Every root-serving source writer must invalidate affected eligibility before effects and reassess/reconcile afterwards; no stored/wire migration is automatic.

- Release note: Adds optional progressive and resumable live lookup routes with a structural provider companion, exact signed capability selection, bounded raw request parsing, fresh authenticated principals, no-store responses and cancellation. configureOutputLookup reuses the existing authentication session and server capacity. Legacy routes, finite lookup behavior and default startup remain unchanged; retained-admission history remains opt-in. Add an optional root-advertisement final HTTP send companion with current data/control authorization and bounded signed reset replacement. Adds explicit authenticated root coordination request/status routes with fatal UTF-8 decoding, original raw byte limits, bounded intake and the shared final-send guard. configureRootEviction integrates them before host parsing, sharing wallet/session authentication and request capacity with existing companions. Adds an optional authenticated proposal router and lazy native configureProposals integration with exact retained response disclosure after signing, shared origin authentication and bounded physical service work. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Adds an optional structural lookup disclosure companion for current-session native enqueue after signing, with one separately authorized sanitized replacement and no retry after an enqueue attempt. Adds an optional private-publication router with exact BRC-103/104 selection, raw UTF-8 bounds, current original-result disclosure, fixed public diagnostics and a single synchronous native enqueue. Adds an authenticated private-acquisition entry and opt-in private acquisition/publication host composition with one session owner and bounded payment headers. Adds opt-in BRC-196 prepare/submit/recover endpoints, sharing host authentication and limits while checking exact private response bytes under the native send gate. Covenant routes reject HTTP payment and preserve legacy submission, acquisition and publication.
- Migration: No migration for existing routes. New lookup support requires SDK 3.0.0, a durable provider companion, a signed matching capability manifest, current authorization and explicitly configured browser origins. Import the standalone adapter from @bsv/overlay-express/output-lookup, or call configureOutputLookup before start. The legacy root loads the adapter lazily. One service binds each concrete base path; do not advertise unsupported profiles. Storage lifecycle and TLS, proxy deadlines and physical authentication capacity remain host responsibilities. Package publication and deployment remain separate authorized actions. The optional root-eviction-response entry requires middleware 2.3.0 and SDK 3.0.0. Capture the shared root revision before reading the complete response, list every disclosed advertisement and install current synchronous data/control access checks. All decision/access writers must share the durable gate. The transport companion resets stale candidates in full; it does not infer targets, mount root routes or retrofit existing lookup/cache/live/GASP paths. No existing route or stored-format migration. The new root-eviction entry is explicitly mounted before generic parsers, compression and caches, with the same origin authentication instance and durable journal as its shared RootEvictionService. Omitted origins preserve credential-free wildcard CORS; explicit arrays opt into exact origins. Native configureRootEviction before start verifies the server wallet identity, inherits host origin policy unless explicitly overridden and clamps bytes to host bounds. The application retains journal/worker lifecycle ownership. Capability publication, scheduler and all serving/admission/GASP fences are separate host obligations. No default route or behavior changes. The new proposals entry requires SDK 3.0 and auth middleware 2.3. Supply the same durable journal to the service and response gate and a current synchronous disclosure policy; mount before parsers and transformations. configureProposals shares host authentication, origin policy and edge bounds. Capability publication and storage/expiry/admission workers remain caller-owned; no default route changes. SDK consumers may retain ^2.4.0 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Lookup send-time protection is opt-in through disclosure on the standalone router or configureOutputLookup, requiring BRC103 and middleware2.3. Existing routes and omitted-option behavior remain unchanged. Import private-publication explicitly with SDK3 and auth middleware2.3; mount before generic parsers or transformations using the same origin authentication instance. Supply the coordinated durable service and disclosure owner; the router does not create a database, start a reconciler, advertise capabilities or install payment handlers. Credential-free CORS remains the default, with explicit origins optional. Existing root imports and routes remain unchanged. No legacy startup change. Configure private services before start with the matching authentication wallet and installed native disclosure owner. Acquisition-configured hosts select a 128-KiB header ceiling; align reverse-proxy limits. The application owns private custody and worker shutdown. Use configurePrivatePurchase or the private-purchase router before body parsers, and supply a durable coordinator/disclosure owner. The application drains its outstanding work before closing protected custody. Basic transport refusal precedes authentication and private work.

## @bsv/overlay-topics

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/overlays/overlay-topics.md](../packages/overlays/overlay-topics.md)
- Source: [packages/overlays/topics](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/overlays/topics)
- Release note: Accepts SDK StorageDownloader UHRP pages up to 200 rows with deterministic outpoint ordering. Retains selector allowlists and authenticated advertisement admission. Removes serial-DID topic/lookup/storage exports and tm_did/ls_did registrations. Existing BRC189 identity discovery, UORA and all other legitimate topics remain. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide. Replaces the tm_mandala/ls_mandala admission, lookup and storage API with Mandala on BRC-162 (BSV-21 binary tokens with authority supply, consuming the @bsv/templates 2.0.0 Bsv21Binary codec): typed MandalaReject refusals with ERR_* codes, the v3 envelope, strict-CBOR admin details committed by the authority output, a trusted-issuer set, an append-only owner journal with inline owner-index repair, and the eviction API. Adds the tm_mandala_registry/ls_mandala_registry identity registry topic (RegistryTopicManager, RegistryLookupService). Changes the persisted Mandala schema (spec section 6.6). UMP lookup requests the retained token-update lineage for presentation, recovery and outpoint queries, within the engine traversal budgets. Advances the packed Overlay dependency for optional retained admission history; retention remains disabled by default.
- Migration: Topics2 is a breaking retirement candidate. Remove DIDTopicManager/createDIDLookupService/DIDRecord/DIDQuery and tm_did/ls_did usage. Resolve immutable identity-key DIDs offline; explicitly configured tm_identity/ls_identity supplies certificate discovery, not DID-document mutation or automatic trust. Preserve existing database/history and plan service rollout without automatic replacement installation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative. Mandala is a clean break with no data migration: the old MandalaToken/MandalaAdmin wire format is no longer admitted and 1.x Mandala rows are not read or converted, so start Mandala on a new database with new deploys (existing on-chain outputs are not spent or deleted). MandalaTopicManager drops adminWallet, adminProtocolID and stateStore.isAdminOutpoint and requires trustedIssuers (non-empty compressed lowercase public keys) and engineOutputs, with optional membership, membershipExempt and onOwnerRepair; pass the same MandalaStorageManager (a MandalaStateStore) to admission and lookup. Refusals are MandalaReject { code, reason } from the Reasons catalog; do not match on old error text. MandalaLinkagePayload is replaced by MandalaEnvelope with encodeEnvelope/decodeEnvelope; the register action is replaced by a deploy at output 0 with a deploySig. foldAction, defaultAssetState, AssetAdminState, FoldContext and MandalaTokenRecord use tokenId (<txid>_0) instead of assetId, drop issuerIdentityKey and add feeRatePerKb. Persisted schema (section 6.6): new mandalaOwners and mandalaAuthorities collections; mandalaTokens, mandalaMetadata, mandalaAssetStates and mandalaAdminHistory are keyed by tokenId, metadata holds the decoded deploy payload, and history rows store kind, detailsHex, commitment and delta (plus optional frozenAmount/frozenOwner on freezes). De-trusting an issuer key revokes the authority coins it holds; rotate keys by moving authority coins first. Operators register tm_mandala_registry/ls_mandala_registry explicitly. The infra/overlay-server wiring follows after publication (P1b). The prior 2.0.0 contracts above are the published baseline. This 2.0.1 UMP patch has no API, wire or schema migration; deploy with overlay 2.6.4 to retain history past confirmation. The optional retained-admission dependency introduces no additional data migration and does not enable retention.

## @bsv/payment-express-middleware

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/middleware/payment-express-middleware.md](../packages/middleware/payment-express-middleware.md)
- Source: [packages/middleware/payment-express-middleware](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/middleware/payment-express-middleware)
- Release note: Removes middleware payment-header size rejection so received payments are validated regardless of header size. Retains the deprecated maxPaymentHeaderBytes option as an ignored source-compatibility field. Atomic BEEF framing, canonical base64, derivation verification, pricing, wallet acceptance and atomic replay protection remain. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: No BRC100 call, wire or wallet-data migration. maxPaymentHeaderBytes is now ignored, including existing explicit values: move transport policy to the HTTP server, CDN, proxy or WAF and remove the deprecated option. Validate the complete HTTP route for supported payment proofs. Published 2.1.8 is verified against protected release 36052862859 and its immutable source artifacts. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

## @bsv/sdk

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/sdk/bsv-sdk.md](../packages/sdk/bsv-sdk.md)
- Source: [packages/sdk](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/sdk)
- Release note: Adds opt-in BRC-192–199 protocol representations, exact encodings, capability selection, live lookup boundaries and closed proposal endpoint codecs while preserving all existing overlay APIs. Adds bounded local capability retention and original-contract revalidation for recovery. Adds bounded common service error envelopes and exact BRC-193 status mappings. Adds explicit AuthFetch automatic-payment opt-out, required mutual authentication and expected server identity controls while preserving existing defaults. Adds a bounded retained-contract BRC-193 HTTP client with authenticated selection binding, cancellation, unpaid errors and caller-owned durable cursor progression. WalletClient and the binary BRC-100 wire no longer reject every acquireCertificate issuance: result validation required the returned fields to equal the request's, but issuance sends plaintext values and the certificate comes back with each value encrypted. An issuance result is now bound to exactly the requested field names; a direct acquisition is still bound to its requested encrypted values exactly. Adds a separate portable BRC-197 exact locking-script, descriptor and revenue-state codec that authenticates the frozen executable before use. Adds separate six-route planning and funded transaction construction with exact mandatory outputs, integer revenue quanta, explicit retirement top-up, externally supplied seller and unanimous recipient transaction signatures, and final-layout binding. Protocol JSON maps explicitly construct own data fields while preserving accepted keys, null prototypes, property attributes and encodings. Adds bounded BRC-195/196 release representations, exact selected-policy binding and registered BRC-77 processor-attestation verification. Adds closed BRC-196 purchase endpoints, signed original-request terms and STEAK/POTATOES status, transaction, recipient and evidence bindings. Adds bounded BRC-195 protected-publication and paid-lookup representations, semantic publication digests and frozen quote, amount, recovery and purchased-output bindings. Adds bounded BRC-195 payment-header parsing, exact single BRC-29 funding-output inspection and proof-independent wallet operation identifiers. Adds bounded BRC-199 signed root request/result and status codecs, exact root/chain/requester and decision bindings, independent restoration bases and explicit new-request clock checks. Adds an opt-in bounded BRC-199 root request/status HTTP client bound to the original signed operation, capability and independently retained policy, with mutual authentication, disabled payments and physical I/O ownership after cancellation. Shares the finite exchange without changing existing lookup transport APIs or diagnostics. Removes the obsolete serial-DID token validation module and deep import. Native identity/certificate, wallet, transaction and authentication behavior is retained. Repairs cold BasePoint/JacobianPoint leaf exports with original-class initialization wrappers and exact declarations. The ESM UMD facade retains the established global effect and canonical class identities; the standalone classic bundle is preserved. Adds the optional retained-operation BRC-194 proposal client with exact publication acknowledgements, signed retrieved author data, active expiry and explicit prior-reservation identity. Adds an explicit authenticated paid-lookup quote/payment/recovery transport with original-operation binding and no automatic payment; malformed bounded payment BEEF is classified invalid. Preserves exact canonical JSON bytes and resource fences while avoiding UTF-8 allocations for printable ASCII chunks and rejecting lone surrogates through Unicode code-point matching; complete Unicode boundary/property evidence remains required. Reuses bounded process-local successful BRC-77 mathematics and canonical valid curve points while rechecking packet representation, digest domain and signer on every call. No packet bodies or authority/currentness decisions are cached. Adds finite authenticated original BRC-196 prepare/submit/recover transport with exact selected recipient/domain/release/transaction bindings and disabled HTTP payments. Its optional identity fence runs inside the existing finite deadline without changing prior paid/lookup/proposal/root behavior. Adds ownOutputJSON for bounded canonical text and independently owned data-only values, preserving all canonical checks and duplicate-aware incoming text/byte parsing. Observes the original authentication response waiter immediately while send is pending, retaining its original timeout, transport failure, exact session removal and listener cleanup. Adds optional purchase commitments and separately retained current-alias evidence to BRC-196 envelopes, with mandatory commitment binding for reserved BRC-197 results and signed POTATOES. Adds full input-zero SHA256d commitment calculation and transparent fixed public child derivation without returning private scalars. These helpers do not qualify the replacement Script/wallet/acquisition integrations, which remain checkpoint-two work. Adds caller-installed completeBoundAction additional-output authorization with exact index, script and amount binding; the default external-input restriction and signed-template verification remain unchanged. Adds a portable RevenueListingProfile codec for the two literal PR295 programs, immutable public-child slots and 717-byte metadata with mandatory height expiry, matching both unchanged positive wire-corpus locks. Complete witness/planner/lineage replacement remains checkpoint-two integration work. Adds separate RevenueListingProfilePlan and RevenueListingProfileSpend entries for immutable activation, purchase, protected-child split, permissionless payout and both retirement routes, with complete source-bound funding, 114/15-value public witnesses and full construction commitments. Complete positive input execution and original 300-run controls cover these components; signed-lineage, native wallet and durable alias integration remain open. Adds an explicitly selected local full-purchase-commitment-v1 transport binding, parser and separate commitment-bound envelope verifier, sharing all existing original-term, recipient, policy, signature and historical release-evidence checks. Adds OutputPurchaseTermsVerifier to own the normalization of a retained original request and selected seller while independently parsing and verifying the complete returned packet, association and BRC77 signature on every call.
- Migration: SDK3 is a separate breaking retirement candidate: remove identity/DIDTokenValidation imports and use @bsv/did BRC202 identity-key resolution plus optional @bsv/did/brc52 original-signature envelopes. Retain historical data and recover authenticated identity bindings; do not relabel serial DIDs. Existing acquisition-result validation fixes remain. First-party SDK3 peer alternatives require complete packed qualification and owner coordination; preserved SDK2 ranges are not silently narrowed. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. The opt-in output APIs preserve existing overlay endpoints and lookup defaults. Select the new versioned profiles explicitly; the accompanying output-knowledge runtime provides durable application state above the SDK. Retained capability records are local replay material: persist them atomically with operations and independently enforce current authorization and operation deadlines. Use allowPayments: false for unpaid authenticated requests. Select requireMutualAuth to disable ordinary HTTP fallback, or expectedIdentityKey to additionally pin the canonical provider key before application dispatch; verify capability/profile bindings separately. Use HTTPS for confidentiality. Omitted controls preserve existing behavior. OutputLookupTransport is opt-in: persist the original opening before dispatch, and atomically commit each batch with its cursor before reading further. Full durable service/runtime integration is separate; no default legacy behavior changes. Import @bsv/sdk/script/templates/RevenueListing explicitly and supply the pinned program bytes; recognition does not establish lineage, currentness, valid spending or fulfillment. The new revenue codec does not alter existing root imports. Opt into RevenueListingPlan/RevenueListingSpend only after domain lineage checks. Supply complete funding predecessors, preserve the planned BRC-100 two-phase layout, obtain raw ALL|FORKID signatures from explicit authorities, and verify the finalized transaction separately; the module never funds, signs or broadcasts by itself. Release-evidence helpers are opt-in: supply independently retained chain, transaction and release policy. Processor verification proves that selected processor signed the exact acceptance statement, not mining or delivery. Mined release still requires authenticated inclusion, selected-chain ancestry and a same-context commit check. No existing wire or stored-data migration. Purchase codecs preserve legacy STEAK and never fund or admit. Authenticate terms against the separately retained request and selected seller, persist them before construction, and supply the exact constructed transaction ID when checking reserved responses. Durable admission, domain/release eligibility and recipient usability remain separate checks. BRC-195 quote/status codecs require authenticated transport and an independently retained selected contract. They do not implement protected storage, wallet internalizeOnce, transaction/release eligibility or secret usability; legacy BRC-105 and lookup context are unchanged. Payment funding inspection requires an independently derived seller payment key, selected chain and retained quote; it does not establish Bitcoin acceptance, reserve an acquisition or internalize wallet value. Enforce total HTTP header limits and use a separate durable idempotent wallet adapter before acknowledging credit. Root-eviction helpers are opt-in and require independently authenticated context, the original signed request and retained evaluation policy. Check clocks only when accepting new requests; retained outcomes remain recoverable under current access policy. Evidence verification, local authority, durable tombstones and every serving/replay guard remain service obligations. Existing SHIP/SLAP, lookup and GASP behavior is unchanged. No migration for existing lookup consumers. Persist original root operation/selection/policy together before constructing OutputRootEvictionTransport; supply trusted root/base/chain/rules and a wallet. The client retries that operation or reads its original status without discovery, persistence, automatic polling or payment. Current access and all serving/evidence decisions remain separate server obligations. Persist the exact proposal request and fresh selected contract before constructing OutputProposalTransport. Each send retries only that saved request. Finalize returns response plus matchesRequest: a different existing reservation is not fulfillment of the requested transaction. Local transport errors remain distinct from authenticated OutputProposalServiceError; domain/evidence verification, current authority, persistence and new-operation freshness remain explicit caller and provider obligations. Existing AuthFetch defaults stay unchanged. Select the new transport explicitly and retain original contracts and payment bytes in a durable owner; see the paid lookup client guide. Existing verification and freshness/authority APIs are unchanged; callers still perform every role, expiry, policy and current-context check. The bounded caches have no persistent data or migration. OutputPurchaseTransport is explicitly selected and requires retained original capability/request/terms and a recipient authentication wallet. Compose durable custody and explicit new-work authorization separately; finite transport never constructs, pays, signs, broadcasts or validates Script/usable private material. The additive ownOutputJSON utility accepts JavaScript values, including strings as values; use parseOutputJSON for incoming JSON text or UTF-8 bytes. Schema, current authorization, wire and storage contracts remain unchanged. The response-waiter lifecycle correction changes no wire format, public API, deadline, automatic payment or session-recovery defaults. Updated opt-in BRC-197 purchases require purchaseCommitment in every reserved result and POTATOES. Pass the independently verified full preimage digest to verifyOutputPurchaseEnvelope as its optional fourth argument; this never relaxes historical txid checks. Independently verify currentAlias BEEF and chain placement before assessing currentness. Other domains and ordinary SDK behavior remain compatible. Public child derivation alone cannot authorize signing, activation or wallet remittance; see docs/guides/revenue-listing-commitments.md. The additive authorization callback requires independently verified local policy; wallet-returned labels or fields are not authority. The completeBoundAction.outputAuthorizationVersion function property allows compatible consumers to detect support without importing a missing named export from older ESM peers. No BRC100 wire or persistence migration is introduced by this addition. New exemplar constructors must use explicit activation or active stages, an immutable initialRevenue schedule without revision, and mandatory expiryHeight. The separately added RevenueListingProfile entry does not reinterpret older descriptors or persisted records, authorize activation or qualify the retained legacy planner; see docs/guides/revenue-listing-profile.md. For the current exemplar, select the ProfilePlan/ProfileSpend entries explicitly, retain mandatory height expiry and immutable schedules, provide complete funding predecessors and at most one final P2PKH change output, and sign only the fixed seller child through the exact protected BRC100 protocol. Planning and construction do not establish signed activation ancestry, Bitcoin/chain acceptance or private release. The earlier single-program/six-route helpers are superseded draft artifacts, not the current specification; their remaining adapter references must be replaced before checkpoint two. Existing verifyOutputPurchaseEnvelope and omitted transport options retain exact-txid behavior. Select commitmentBinding explicitly for submit/recover with matching original signed domain and retained complete original funded candidate. Preparation cannot select it; no request body or HTTP payment changes. Independently verify both complete transactions and their same full commitment before accepting rights; SDK transport binding does not establish Script, alias, chain or secret usability, or migrate native buyer/wallet custody. The additive OutputPurchaseTermsVerifier is optional. Its verify method repeats all response checks and retains no response or verification verdict. The existing verifyOutputPurchaseTerms signature and checks remain unchanged; current domain, authorization and fulfillment checks remain separate.

## @bsv/simple

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/helpers/simple.md](../packages/helpers/simple.md)
- Source: [packages/helpers/simple](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/helpers/simple)
- Release note: Corrects PushDrop self-derivation ownership, pins Message Box responses to the authenticated peer, hardens wallet, credential, DID, persistence, and transaction boundaries, preserves explicit offline migration identifiers and historical signature verification for pre-0.6 short certificate types while keeping new issuance, remote metadata, and wallet operations canonical 32-byte, and changes the generated server-wallet handler to require explicit authenticated action-level authorization. Preserves original BRC52 signed bytes, including the SDK certificate serializer's existing field order; persisted local field ordering remains a separate concern. Replaces mutable serial DID tooling with offline identity-key DID adapters and copied VC/VP proof wrappers with original-signature-preserving BRC52 envelopes. Retains certificate issuance/acquisition/revocation and persisted data.
- Migration: Simple0.7 is a breaking pre-1.0 candidate. Remove mutable DID/resolver/provider configuration, proxy handlers and DIDError/types; use DID.fromIdentityKey/resolve and wallet.getDID. CredentialIssuer.issue returns {credential,keyringForSubject}; verify accepts exact JSON or UTF8 bytes and returns structured cryptographic results. The HTTP verify route now requires {credential: originalEnvelopeJson} with original text as a string; parsed objects return HTTP400. Web request decoding rejects duplicate members and invalid UTF8, and custom parsed-body adapters must establish equivalent strict decoding. Preserve received text and inspect verification.verified, not HTTP success. Local revocation record status is retained/unknown, not inferred chain revocation. See docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. Replace createServerWalletHandler() deployments with createServerWalletHandler({ authorize: async ({ action, headers }) => authenticatedSessionCanUseAction(headers, action) }). The callback must return literal true for each status, create, request, receive, balance, outputs, or reset action; omission now returns HTTP 403 for every action. Roll out the authentication layer and callback with the package, update anonymous probes or automation, and apply the same policy to every replica. Do not emulate the old public behavior with an unconditional authorize: () => true callback. Valid recipient derivations and authenticated Message Box peers remain supported; malformed, wrong-owner, or transaction-mutated flows now fail closed. New CredentialSchema and Certifier records use canonical 32-byte types. Current SDK wallet methods reject historical short types, so do not put migration aliases in wallet list, acquire, prove, or relinquish calls. Export affected records through the storage version that created them, authenticate them offline against the exact locally configured identifier, and reissue/import canonical replacements; no legacy certificate is rewritten automatically. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/. Persisted local field ordering requires no migration; transport adapters preserve original certificate signing bytes.

## @bsv/templates

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/helpers/templates.md](../packages/helpers/templates.md)
- Source: [packages/helpers/ts-templates](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/helpers/ts-templates)
- Release note: Templates 2.0.0 replaces the Mandala token format with BRC-162 (BSV-21 binary) token outputs. Adds Bsv21Binary: an encoder and decoder for the BRC-162 prefix (token id, amount, optional payload) in front of any locking script, with exactly one accepted encoding per value (32-byte id as a direct push; amount OP_0, OP_1..OP_16 or a minimal direct push; amounts as bigint up to 2^64-1), role helpers, <txid>_0 token-id strings, lock/lockBRC29 and a P2PKH unlock. Adds a hand-rolled strict DAG-CBOR subset codec (encodeStrictCbor/decodeStrictCbor) with no new runtime dependency, safe in CommonJS and ESM. Includes the 1.10.3 CommonJS interop fix (issue #571): SDK classes are imported by name from the SDK barrels. Removes MandalaToken, MandalaAdmin and ADMIN_PROTOCOL. Also publishes the SDK 3 peer alternative already declared in source (superseded 1.10.4 candidate, PR #729): @bsv/sdk ^2.1.6 || ^3.0.0.
- Migration: Breaking. Removed exports: MandalaToken, MandalaTokenDecoded, MandalaAdmin, ADMIN_PROTOCOL, MandalaAdminDecoded, MandalaActionDetails, MandalaActionKind, MandalaAdminLockParams, MandalaAdminUnlockParams and AssetMetadata. Removed subpath @bsv/templates/mandala-signing.ts. The @bsv/templates/mandala-encoding.ts subpath keeps only createMinimallyEncodedScriptChunk, decodeScriptNum and decodeScriptNumChunk; encodeScriptNum, encodeAssetId and decodeAssetId are removed. Replace MandalaToken/MandalaAdmin with Bsv21Binary: deploy, authority and value outputs are lock(tokenId | null, amount, pubKeyHash, payload?) with bigint amounts and <txid>_0 token ids (tokenIdFromString/tokenIdToString), decoded with Bsv21Binary.decode. Mandala admin actions are committed by sha256 of strict-CBOR details in the authority output payload, not by a commitment-derived key. This is a clean break with no data migration: tokens and admin chains in the old format are not readable by 2.0.0. @bsv/overlay-topics 2.0.0 consumes this format; the infra/overlay-server wiring follows after publication. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the SDK3 candidate; SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API (see docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md).

## @bsv/teranode-listener

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/network/teranode-listener.md](../packages/network/teranode-listener.md)
- Source: [packages/network/ts-p2p](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/network/ts-p2p)
- Release note: Adds optional bounded decoding for Teranode's two-layer JSON message envelope and typed topic payload interfaces. Hardens the network boundary with canonical PNET, multiaddr, topic, configuration, callback, and numeric validation; immutable caller-owned inputs; exact runtime controls; coalesced retry-safe lifecycle transitions; and a working DHT-disable control. Replaces the internal placeholder subtree hash with the canonical Bitcoin Merkle root and verifies exact uint64 values, dimensions, totals, conflicts, framing, and resource ceilings before accepting serialized subtree state. Refreshes the compatible libp2p dependency set while retaining the imported source's hash-pinned MIT provenance and notices. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: No API migration is required for valid consumers: raw callbacks remain the default and decoding is opt-in with decodeMessages: true. Configuration arrays and callbacks are snapshotted at construction, boolean controls must be literal booleans, and malformed or duplicate topics, addresses, keys, and unsupported properties now fail closed. usePrivateDHT: false now actually omits the DHT service. The published mainnet PNET value is transport compatibility data, not a publisher credential; decoded sender and payload fields remain untrusted and security-critical claims require independent validation. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

Valid canonical transaction-builder flows remain supported; malformed, ambiguous, or wallet-mutated results now fail closed. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package. SDK consumers may retain ^2.1.6 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. ## @bsv/wallet-relay

- Package documentation: [docs/packages/wallet/wallet-relay.md](../packages/wallet/wallet-relay.md)
- Source: [packages/wallet/ts-wallet-relay](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/wallet/ts-wallet-relay)
- Release note: Adds the strict package contract and preserves wallet RPC, encrypted relay payloads, signatures, and transaction bytes across number-array, Uint8Array, Buffer, and historical numeric-key JSON runtimes. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Enforces signed pairing metadata before relay resolution, requires HTTPS outside loopback development for pairing origins and directly configured relay APIs, and rejects privileged wallet methods when no explicit approval callback is configured. Retains portable wallet RPC byte handling and the strict package contract. Tolerates two missed heartbeat pongs by default and adds close diagnostics whose callback failures cannot interrupt disconnect cleanup. Hardens both wallet-RPC trust boundaries with exact argument and security-sensitive result validation; serializes sequence acceptance and outbound encryption; prevents stale mobile lifecycle work, reconnect identity squatting, active-socket authorization after expiry, and shutdown races; makes session lifetime absolute; and bounds concurrent wallet requests, log retention, response bodies, session capacity, and creation rate. Restricts active QR artifacts, pairing-URI structure, and scaffold output paths; adds no-store bearer-response policy, constant-time desktop-token checks, safe browser WebSocket subprotocol authentication, deterministic relay teardown, fail-closed callback containment, strict scaffold request parsing, and corrected wallet-authentication UI semantics. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while preserving the existing SDK2 lower bound; clean packed SDK2.8.11 and SDK3 candidate consumers are documented in the identity/DID/VC migration guide.
- Migration: Enable signed QR codes and distribute only HTTPS pairing origins and relay API URLs. Root-relative API paths and loopback HTTP remain supported. Configure onApprovalRequired for every method not deliberately listed in autoApproveMethods; unsigned pairing URIs and implicit approval are no longer accepted. Existing relay sessions, custom RPC method names, and supported wallet RPC byte encodings remain valid, and host applications continue to provide their matching Express runtime and type graph. Version 0.5 defaults to two missed pongs; set maxMissedHeartbeats to 1 to retain the prior heartbeat policy. Heartbeat intervals must fit the Node timer range. Preserve Cache-Control: no-store at proxies, prefer the stable bsv-wallet-relay plus token WebSocket subprotocols over the legacy token query parameter, and configure edge rate limiting in addition to the bounded in-process defaults. The 24-hour connected-session lifetime no longer renews on reconnect, malformed wallet calls fail with code 400, and WalletRelayClient retains at most 100 log entries unless maxLogEntries is configured. The QR remains a short-lived bearer invitation: keep it private and require explicit operation approval. Relay envelopes, cryptographic framing, and wallet RPC encodings remain unchanged. SDK consumers may retain ^2.4.1 or install the proposed SDK3 candidate. The immutable SDK2.8.11 reference has nine pre-existing SDK cold-leaf/UMD import defects; all historical floor versions are not qualified by this matrix. SDK3 removes the obsolete DID token API; use the identity-key DID and optional BRC52 adapters described in docs/guides/identity-did-vc-migration.md. No other public API or wire migration is introduced by the peer alternative.

CLI entry points: `{"wallet-relay":"./bin/init.mjs"}`.
