- Source: [packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox](https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/ts-stack/tree/main/packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox)
- Release note: WalletPermissionsManager retires signed no-send ownership and reference aliases after createAction or signAction reports sending or unproven, including sendWith-only calls and successful members of an undelayed review error. Failed or unreported actions retain their originator binding for retry or abort. Cleanup visits only the retired transaction's references and preserves aliases reused by newer actions. Adds an SDK3 peer alternative while retaining the existing SDK2.8.0 floor. Public Argon2id declarations reference the typed hash-wasm package while retaining the same generic binary/string contract and emitted runtime bytes. Fixes WAB faucet redemption for an empty wallet when storage adds a service charge. Local signer decisions for independently validated commission and derived change are retained privately through the permissions wrapper and bound by the SDK before signing. UMP pins anchor verified token-update lineage: password and token updates supersede their pinned predecessor, while unrelated historical continuations cannot override the anchor. Explicit overlay history is linked past confirmed Merkle anchors. Updates with missing pin ancestry remain indeterminate instead of selecting an unrelated continuation. Every retained token spend proves control through its unlocking script, including confirmed updates and hash rotation; funding paths do not establish token lineage. Optional local SQLite controllers additionally retain exact two-phase noSend allocation/signing state and atomically reconcile one BRC-29 funding output with wallet ownership, deferred monitor work and a durable receipt. The new deep imports do not add root exports or BRC-100 RPC methods. Private recovery JSON and binary encoding now use separate internal modules with unchanged accepted bytes, exports and bounds. Recoverable noSend finalization accepts an optional synchronous current-authority guard for new signing; an existing exact final remains recoverable after expiry. The native recoverable action controller adds a synchronous read-only configuration descriptor for binding an opt-in original-payment adapter to its actual wallet, storage, network and originator; existing action behavior and RPC contracts are unchanged. Local recovery JSON ownership is factored into an internal call-local scalar, array and record context, preserving the original byte, depth, item, Unicode, descriptor and cycle rules. Adds an explicitly selected local BRC-197 fixed-child intake capability and complete existing signer/storage pipeline; ordinary BRC-29 validation, BRC-100 wire behavior, schema and defaults remain unchanged. This reference capability remains under native and end-to-end qualification.
- Migration: No public API, wire, database, or consumer migration is required. Pending no-send actions and retryable failures retain the same originator-bound abort behavior; positively queued or broadcast actions no longer retain session ownership records. Upgrade the SDK to a release exposing completeBoundAction.outputAuthorizationVersion=1 alongside wallet-toolbox 2.14.6. SDK2 peers keep their existing strict behavior; they do not obtain this fee-bearing faucet fix. The main SDK3.1 candidate retains the separate SDK3 retirement migration; SDK2 hosts require a coordinated additive backport or that migration. Serialized or cross-package-instance result adapters discard local authority and fail closed. Signup interruption/retry persistence is unchanged; reconcile any previous faucet transaction before repeating a failed signup. No API or schema migration is required for pin continuity. Retire a support pin only after unpinned lookup independently returns the verified current token. Deploy overlay 2.6.4 plus overlay-topics 2.0.1 or an equivalent history decider for confirmed ancestry. Stored WAB pins remain lineage anchors; the client follows verified descendants without needing an administrative pin rewrite. For ordinary callers, no public API, wire, database, or consumer migration is required. Recovery adoption requires SDK 3.0.0, explicit auxiliary schema installation in the active local SQLite wallet, stable operation IDs and a committed workspace. Reopen retained state after restart; never silently reinstall a missing journal. These journals are outside legacy entity snapshots, BRC-38/39 export, ordinary sync, IndexedDB and remote providers. Back up the whole consistent wallet database plus keys and test restoration. For rollback, stop new adoption and reconcile outstanding operations with the original controller before removing it; preserve journals and keys. Local receipts do not establish quote-time capacity, settlement, domain authority or protected delivery. The private encoder extraction requires no caller or stored-format migration; complete canonical mutation qualification covers every helper. Existing callers can omit checkNewSigning. The optional callback returns void synchronously or throws, and cannot undo or timestamp already-started storage effects; reconcile the original operation after uncertainty. This internal ownership refactor changes no accepted bytes, public action API, stored schema, errors or caller defaults; no additional migration is required and context is never retained between calls. BRC-197 integrations must explicitly select getBrc197InternalizationCapabilities and internalizeBrc197Action with the literal fixed remittance fields; do not Base64-encode them or route them through ordinary internalizeAction. Validate every recipient and the complete protected activation/signing, lineage, chain, fee and resource prerequisites before funding a listing. See docs/guides/brc197-fixed-child-wallet.md for the local-only boundary and outstanding qualification gates.

## Change procedure

1. Change the public package and select the SemVer impact from its packed API,
   runtime, wire, persistence, and declaration changes.
2. Bump only affected package manifests and first-party dependents whose packed
   contract changes.
3. Update the matching entry in
   `governance/package-release-notes.json`, including explicit migration
   guidance even when no consumer action is required.
4. Run `pnpm docs:packages`, `pnpm docs:packages:check`,
   `pnpm check-versions`, packed-consumer checks, and the full release gates.
5. After an authorized publication, update `publishedVersion` to the registry
   result and set `releaseType` to `none` only when source and npm match.
